rot.worstPiece.ideia.london.e1: Attack: this position comes from a London. White has brought the bishop to g3 and the knights to f3 and d2, and Black has castled. Neither side has a check, a threat or a capture that wins material.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.london.e2: When that happens, look for the piece doing the least and take it to a better square. The bishop on f1 has not left home and still blocks castling. On d3 it would aim at h7, near the black king.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.london.l1: Black improves too: the pawn goes to c5 and attacks the d4 pawn.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.london.l2: White defends d4 with the pawn on c3. The knight went to d2, not c3, precisely to leave that square free for the pawn.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.london.l3: The black knight comes out and attacks d4 a second time. The d4 pawn has three defenders: the pawns on c3 and e3 and the knight on f3.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.london.l4: Now the f1 bishop comes out: on d3 it aims at h7, near the black king, and clears the way for castling.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.london.l5: No move here won material. Each side brought out the piece that was doing the least. With no tactic in the position, that is usually the plan.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.torre.e1: Attack: another position, from a Lichess game. No check or capture wins anything right now. Which white piece is doing the least? The rook on h1 has not left home yet.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.torre.e2: The rook on d4 attacks the knight on d6, defended only by the rook on d8. The knight cannot move: if it does, the d4 rook captures the d8 rook.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.torre.p: Find the move that brings the h1 rook into play.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.torre.certo: The rook goes to d1, behind the d4 rook. Now the knight has two attackers and one defender, and it still cannot move.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.torre.revela: The h1 rook goes to d1, behind the d4 rook: two attackers against the knight, which has only one defender and cannot move.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.torre.err.c1b2.1: After this move, the king attacks the a2 bishop, but it retreats to e6 and now covers c4: if the rook goes to d1, the knight leaves d6 with check on c4.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.torre.err.c1b2.2: Back to the position: the h1 rook is still not playing. Look for a useful square for it.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.torre.err.c1c2.1: After this move, the a2 bishop goes to c4 and then to d3 with check, and closes the d-file to your rooks.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.torre.err.c1c2.2: Back to the position: the h1 rook is still not playing. Look for a useful square for it.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.torre.err.g2g4.1: After this move, the black king goes to f6 and then to e7, and starts defending the knight.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.torre.err.g2g4.2: Back to the position: the h1 rook is still not playing. Look for a useful square for it.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.torre.err.h2h3.1: After this move, the black king goes to f7 and then to e7, and starts defending the knight.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.torre.err.h2h3.2: Back to the position: the h1 rook is still not playing. Look for a useful square for it.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.torre.err.d4d6.1: The rook captures the knight, but the d8 rook recaptures: White gives a rook for a knight.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.torre.err.d4d6.2: Back to the position: before capturing, add one more attacker against the knight.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.torre.fora: That move does not bring the h1 rook into play. Look for a move with it.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.torre.volta: Try again: take the h1 rook to a useful file.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.torre.l0: Black cannot defend the knight again in time.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.torre.l1: The black rook leaves the d-file: that way, at least, it is not captured after the knight.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.torre.l2: The rook captures the knight. White has won a piece.
rot.worstPiece.ideia.torre.l3: The h1 rook was doing nothing. Brought to the d-file, it added an attacker, and the knight fell. Improving the worst piece often creates the tactic.
rot.worstPiece.demos.regra.1: Attack demonstration: a Lichess game. The d1 rook stands behind White's own d4 pawn: on the d-file it only defends that pawn. It is White's worst piece.
rot.worstPiece.demos.regra.2: On the h-file, the h3 rook attacks the knight on h7. The knight is pinned: behind it is the black king, its only defender.
rot.worstPiece.demos.regra.3: The d1 rook goes to h1 and doubles on the h-file: two attackers against the knight. The d4 pawn is left undefended, but the knight is worth more.
rot.worstPiece.demos.regra.4: The king goes to g7 and unpins the knight, but it is White's turn, and the knight still has two attackers and only one defender.
rot.worstPiece.demos.regra.5: The rook captures the knight with check. The king cannot recapture: the h1 rook defends h7.
rot.worstPiece.demos.regra.6: The king steps out of check.
rot.worstPiece.demos.regra.7: The rook that only defended a pawn went to the file where there was a target, and White won the knight. The target can also be the king: near it, the improved piece can threaten mate.
rot.worstPiece.demos.regra2.1: Attack demonstration: now let us think from Black's side, in another Lichess game. The h8 rook has not left home yet: it is Black's worst piece.
rot.worstPiece.demos.regra2.2: The d6 rook attacks the knight on d2. It is pinned: behind it is the white king, its only defender.
rot.worstPiece.demos.regra2.3: The h8 rook goes to d8 and doubles on the d-file: two attackers against the knight.
rot.worstPiece.demos.regra2.4: The king goes to e1 and unpins the knight, but it is Black's turn, and the knight still has two attackers and only one defender.
rot.worstPiece.demos.regra2.5: The rook captures the knight. The king cannot recapture, because the d8 rook defends d2.
rot.worstPiece.demos.regra2.6: Again, the piece that was not playing added an attacker, and the pinned knight fell.
rot.worstPiece.demos.rei.1: Attack demonstration: White again, in another Lichess game. The h6 queen is already near the black king, but alone it threatens nothing: the king defends g7.
rot.worstPiece.demos.rei.2: The g3 knight does nothing. From h5, it would attack g7 together with the queen.
rot.worstPiece.demos.rei.3: The knight goes to h5 and threatens mate: the queen goes to g7, protected by the knight, and the king cannot recapture.
rot.worstPiece.demos.rei.4: The black queen goes to f6 and defends g7.
rot.worstPiece.demos.rei.5: The knight captures the queen, with check.
rot.worstPiece.demos.rei.6: The idle piece went near the king and created a mate threat. To defend, Black lost the queen.
rot.worstPiece.demos.excecao.1: Attack demonstration: now the exception, in another Lichess game. White has not castled yet, and the rooks have not left home. Castling would bring the h1 rook out of the corner.
rot.worstPiece.demos.excecao.2: But before improving a piece, check the checks, the captures and the threats. The g6 pawn has no defender, and the d3 queen and the e5 knight attack it.
rot.worstPiece.demos.excecao.3: The queen captures the pawn with check.
rot.worstPiece.demos.excecao.4: The king only has f8 to get out of check.
rot.worstPiece.demos.excecao.5: The queen, defended by the e5 knight, mates on f7.
rot.worstPiece.demos.excecao.6: Had White castled, the h8 rook would go to g8 and defend the pawn. Improving the worst piece is the plan when there is no tactic; first, check whether the position has one.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.valeAqui.enunciad: Now let us think from Black's side. Your b8 knight and a8 rook have not left home yet. Is it worth improving one of them now? Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.valeAqui.fim: The rook went to g6 and threatened mate with the queen on g1, defended by the rook. To close the g-file, White gave up the queen on g4, and the pawn captured it. Before the knight, there was a threat to make.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.valeAqui.err.b8d7: The knight comes out, but the move threatens nothing: White moves the f1 bishop and brings a rook to g1, against your queen. Before the knight, check what your queen threatens on the g-file.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.valeAqui.err.e6e5: The pawn advances, but White plays the pawn to c5 and gives check with the bishop on c4. Before any plan, check what your queen threatens on the g-file.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.valeAqui.err.g5h4: The queen leaves the g-file, and White plays the pawn to f3 against your e4 pawn. Before any plan, check what your queen threatens on the g-file.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.valeAqui.err.f6f7: The rook retreats without threatening anything, and White plays the pawn to f3 and captures your e4 pawn. Before any plan, check what your queen threatens on the g-file.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.valeAqui.err.b7b5: The pawn advances, but White brings the bishop to g2 and a rook to g1, against your queen. Before any plan, check what your queen threatens on the g-file.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.valeAqui.errPos.g: The queen retreats, and the white queen escapes to f4. White has given up the queen on g4: capture it with the least valuable piece.
Your queen captures the queen, but the h3 pawn recaptures, and White is still a bishop up. Capture with the least valuable piece.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.torre.enunciado: Play as White and find the best move.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.torre.fim: The a1 rook went to d1 and added an attacker against the d3 knight, held by the d8 rook. The black rook went to d5, but the knight still had only one defender and fell.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.torre.err.g1f1: The king goes to f1, but the d3 knight escapes to c5 and is safe. Look for a useful square for the rook that has not played yet.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.torre.err.d2d1: The rook retreats, and the black d8 rook goes to d5 and defends the knight from close by. Look for a useful square for the rook that has not played yet.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.torre.err.d2d3: The rook captures the knight, but the d8 rook recaptures: White gives a rook for a knight. Before capturing, add one more attacker.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.torre.err.a3a4: The pawn advances, but the d3 knight captures the e5 pawn and gets out of the attack. Look for a useful square for the rook that has not played yet.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.torre.err.f3d4: The knight goes to d4, but the d3 knight captures the e5 pawn and gets out of the attack. Look for a useful square for the rook that has not played yet.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.torrePreta.enunci: Now let us think from Black's side. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.torrePreta.fim: The f8 rook went to the c-file and added an attacker against the c1 knight, which defended the e2 bishop. The knight got out of the attack, the bishop was left undefended, and the rook captured it.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.torrePreta.err.f8: The f8 rook comes out, but on the a-file it finds no target. Look for the file where it adds an attacker.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.torrePreta.errPos: The e2 bishop was left undefended, but the move does not capture it, and White pulls it back to f1. Capture it now, while you can.
The e2 bishop was left undefended, but the move does not capture it, and White pulls it back to f1. Capture it now, while you can.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.torrePreta.err.g8: The move threatens nothing, and White brings the d4 rook to d2 to challenge your c2 rook. Look for a useful square for the rook that has not played yet.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.torrePreta.err.h7: The move threatens nothing, and White brings the d4 rook to d2 to challenge your c2 rook. Look for a useful square for the rook that has not played yet.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.torrePreta.err.a6: The move threatens nothing, and White brings the d4 rook to d2 to challenge your c2 rook. Look for a useful square for the rook that has not played yet.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.torrePreta.err.c2: The c2 rook leaves the second rank, and White brings the d4 rook to d3 to trade it. Before moving the rook that already works, activate the f8 rook.
rot.worstPiece.pratica.torrePreta.errPos: The rook goes to c3, but the knight goes to c5, and the e2 bishop is still standing. Look at the bishop: it has been left undefended.
